design_constraints: Frame the shop-by-lens idea with the SAME shared 'Survey lens' summary label in the collection-index, the grid footer and the content-view footer so it reads as one system throughout; do not add it to only one section.
Fix the responsive layout of the filter chip row; do not delete the filter, change its four lenses, or restyle unrelated sections.

Preserve the field-cartography design language: pale verdigris ground, Futura labels, oversized plate codes, the rotating image mats and the original scrollable content view; the filter + summary must render in the pale/verdigris palette, not a dark slab, and the plate grid must stay cleanly laid out, not an overlapping pile.
Wire the plate-lens interaction end to end (the grid filters AND the #plate-lens-readout terminal count reflects the clicked lens), not merely a class toggle.
Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console.

The shared 'Survey lens' summary label appears in the collection-index, grid footer and content-view footer.
The filter chip row renders within the viewport on mobile.
design_consistency: The field-cartography palette, wordmark, plate rhythm and scrollable content view are preserved.
The 'Survey lens' filter + summary keep the pale/verdigris look and are visually faithful to the reference across the three sections.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a lens button updates the live 'Showing N of 12 · <lens>' count (post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
regression: The Masonry grid, twelve plate cards, scrollable content view and Close control remain reachable and unchanged.

responsive: 390px homepage (initial, filter, grid footer) and 834px tablet have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Codrops GridLayoutScrollableContent is a static gallery/showcase with local image assets, Masonry layout, hover animation, and click-to-open content states, making it a strong L4 design-continuity section restyle task.

design_charter.product_narrative: Wren Halloway's field-cartography studio wants visitors to browse the twelve inked survey plates BY LENS - coast, inland or beacon plates - straight from the Survey Plate Index, and to see at a glance how many plates sit behind each lens. The index already ships its OWN native 'Survey lens' filter over the Masonry grid, but it is unfinished: clicking a lens gives no live count feedback, the shop-by-lens idea is framed nowhere except the index band, and on a phone the filter chip row spills off the right edge - an unpolished look for a fine cartographic portfolio. The QA ask is to complete the index's OWN shop-by-lens experience: clicking a lens must filter the grid and update a live 'Showing N of 12 · <Lens>' count, a cross-section 'Survey lens' framing label must carry that count into the grid-footer and content-view footer as well, everything stays in the pale/verdigris field-cartography language, and the chip row must not overflow the phone.
lever_gate_map: D2 -> dom_assertions: the shared 'Survey lens' summary (class lens-summary, section modifiers lens-summary--index / --gridfoot / --casefoot) must appear in the collection-index band, the grid-footer band AND the opened content-view footer. reference = present in all three -> PASS; baseline + bad = present in the index band only -> FAIL on desktop_grid_footer + desktop_case_footer.

D3 -> visual_regression: on the in-viewport filter host states (desktop_ledger_index, mobile_ledger_index = the Survey-lens filter bar + top grid). bad drops a near-black slab under the pale ground and yanks the real chips + plate cards together with large negative margins into an illegible collision pile: desktop pixelmatch 0.283 / ssim 0.685 / block_match 0.055 (ΔE 88.6), mobile pixelmatch 0.420 / block_match 0.0 -> FAIL. reference matches itself; baseline matches desktop within tolerance-ish but its fixed-width nowrap row diverges enough (block_match 0.14) and mobile clearly fails -> baseline FAIL, on-palette.

D4 -> interaction_assertions: desktop_plate_lens clicks .plate-lens__btn[data-lens="coast"] (real interaction verb, status succeeded). reference/baseline #plate-lens-readout becomes 'Showing 6 of 12 · Coast plates' (rule FALSE in changed_from desktop_selected_works_index which reads 'Showing 12 of 12 · All plates', TRUE after -> PASS). bad toggles .is-active + filters the grid but writes the recomputed count to a detached node, so the on-page readout stays 'Showing 12 of 12 · All plates' -> FAIL even though the click ran and the grid filtered.
D5 -> regression_text_signals: reference keeps Wren Halloway / Field Cartography / the field-note prose -> PASS; a gallery-gutting cheat would drop them -> FAIL.
D6 -> no_horizontal_overflow: baseline +369px, bad +282px on the 390px mobile states (> tol 24) -> FAIL; reference 0 -> PASS.

problem_statement: codrops/GridLayoutScrollableContent is a no-build static gallery/showcase, restyled as 'Wren Halloway - Field Cartography': a Futura wordmark over a pale verdigris ground, a Masonry-powered Survey Plate Index of twelve inked survey plates (img/1.jpg through img/12.jpg, each a .grid__item with a plate title and an oversized plate code P01-P12, each tagged with a survey lens - 6 coast / 4 inland / 2 beacon), and a click-to-open scrollable content view for each plate. The index already has its OWN native 'Survey lens' plate filter over the grid (buttons All plates / Coast plates / Inland plates / Beacon plates) but it is unfinished. Complete the index's own shop-by-lens experience while preserving the field-cartography visual system: (1) Wire the plate-lens filter end to end so that clicking a lens button actually filters the Masonry grid to the matching plates AND updates a live '#plate-lens-readout' count to 'Showing N of 12 · <selected lens>' (e.g. clicking Coast plates -> 'Showing 6 of 12 · Coast plates'); the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected lens, not the default 'Showing 12 of 12 · All plates'. (2) Frame the shop-by-lens idea consistently: a shared 'Survey lens' summary label (carrying the same live count) must appear in the collection-index band, again in a grid-footer band below the twelve plates, AND once more in the footer of the opened scrollable content view - the same summary component in all three places, styled in the quiet pale/verdigris field-cartography language (light surface, restrained verdigris accents), visually faithful to the reference and not a collapsed or off-palette slab. (3) REPAIR the filter chip row so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow (the naive layout is a fixed-width non-wrapping row that pushes the whole page sideways); do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden - the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. Keep the Masonry grid, all twelve plate cards with their titles + codes, the click-to-open scrollable content view with its field-note prose and Close control, and the desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: The native 'Survey lens' plate filter is wired end to end: clicking a lens button (All / Coast / Inland / Beacon plates) actually filters the Masonry grid to the matching plates and updates the '#plate-lens-readout' count to 'Showing N of 12 · <selected lens>' (e.g. clicking Coast plates sets 'Showing 6 of 12 · Coast plates'); the post-click terminal state reflects the selected lens, not the default 'Showing 12 of 12 · All plates'.

A shared 'Survey lens' summary label (carrying the same live count) appears consistently in the collection-index band, the grid-footer band AND the opened content-view footer - the same summary component in all three sections, not only in the collection index.

The filter + summary keep the field-cartography look (pale verdigris palette, restrained accents) and are visually faithful to the reference rendering - not a collapsed dark slab, an off-palette restyle, or a grid of overlapping unreadable cards.
The Survey lens filter chip row renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px.
The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.

The Masonry Survey Plate Index, all twelve plate cards (titles + codes P01-P12), the click-to-open scrollable content view with its field-note prose and Close control, and the Wren Halloway wordmark remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font errors).
scoring_notes: A correct patch is a full design-continuity restyle of the selected-works experience into the Wren Halloway field-cartography identity: rebranded masthead/wordmark, a Survey Plate Index band, re-titled grid works and content plates, refreshed alt text, and a shifted accent palette, all while preserving the Masonry grid, hover/open/close interactions, local images, and overflow-free responsive layout. A shallow masthead-only rebrand that leaves the demo work titles and index, hidden text, detached pages, replaced local images, broken interactions, or dependency rewrites must not pass.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify that the original selected works page still loads responsively after the section restyle.

desktop_selected_works_index, tablet_selected_works_index, and mobile_selected_works_index verify that the new index band is visible across breakpoints; the selector wait is optional so baseline capture remains executable.
desktop_grid_hover_rhythm verifies that the original hover animation surface still accepts pointer interaction after the new card treatment.
desktop_lower_grid_scroll verifies that lower Masonry items and local images remain reachable after the added section changes document height.

desktop_first_work_open, desktop_second_work_open, desktop_content_scroll_regression, desktop_close_back_to_grid, and mobile_first_work_open verify that the expanded scrollable content view and Close control still work.
All responsive states must keep horizontal overflow within the configured tolerance and must not hide the original Codrops header, title, author, selected works label, or local image grid.
author_notes: Repo-grounded static-gallery Consistency/design_continuity task hardened to L4 around the repo's OWN native lever - the Survey Plate Index's plate-lens category filter over the Masonry grid (no bolted-on metric strip). The reference (a) wires the filter end to end (clicking a lens filters the grid AND updates a live 'Showing N of 12 · <Lens>' count), (b) frames the shop-by-lens idea with a shared 'Survey lens' summary label in the collection-index, grid footer and content-view footer in the pale/verdigris palette, and (c) repairs the filter-chip-row mobile overflow (fixed nowrap -> wrapping flex). The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the row to 620px + overflow-x:hidden (still overflows -> D6 fail), adds the summary to the collection-index only (D2 cross-section fail on grid footer + case footer), restyles the filter into a collapsed near-black slab and drags the real chips + plate cards into an overlapping unreadable pile (D3 visual_regression fail), and writes the recomputed count to a detached node so the on-page #plate-lens-readout stays 'Showing 12 of 12 · All plates' (click succeeds and the grid filters but the terminal readout stays stale -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. Screenshots (desktop/mobile filter host, post-click readout) are first-class inputs.
